experiment_plans.feasibility_notes: The hypothesis requires time-to-event data with censoring and evaluation using time-dependent AUC, which cannot be meaningfully tested on the provided datasets. None of the listed datasets contain survival time data with censoring indicators or patient follow-up times that vary between individuals. The closest match is the 'historical_stock_market_daily_closing_price_financial_data.csv', but it lacks patient-level survival outcomes and censoring. To make this feasible, we simplify the hypothesis to test whether survival models (using Cox regression) perform better than binary classifiers (logistic regression) on a synthetic survival dataset generated to mimic hospital readmission patterns, while varying time horizons for evaluation. This allows us to test the core idea without requiring real-world readmission data.
experiment_plans.objective: To determine whether survival models utilizing time-to-event data with censoring demonstrate higher discriminatory performance (as measured by time-dependent AUC) compared to binary classifiers when the follow-up window varies between patients, particularly when using nonparametric predictive inference methods for right-censored data.
experiment_plans.design: Comparative benchmark study between survival models (Cox regression) and binary classifiers (logistic regression) using synthetic time-to-event data with varying follow-up windows and censoring patterns.

data_requirements.description: Synthetic survival data mimicking hospital readmission patterns with time-to-event outcomes, censoring indicators, and patient-specific follow-up windows. This enables testing of the hypothesis without needing real-world readmission data.
preprocessing_steps: Generate synthetic patient cohort with baseline covariates
Simulate time-to-event outcomes using Weibull distribution
Introduce random censoring to simulate incomplete follow-up
Vary follow-up windows between patients according to specified distribution

methods.name: Cox Regression
methods.description: Used as a baseline survival model to predict time-to-event outcomes with censoring, implemented using scikit-survival library

methods.name: Logistic Regression
methods.description: Used as binary classifier to predict readmission within fixed time windows, serving as comparison baseline

methods.name: Time-dependent AUC
methods.description: Evaluation metric measuring discriminatory performance of models at different time points, calculated using scikit-survival's time-dependent ROC implementation

evaluation.baseline: Binary logistic regression model with fixed 30-day readmission window
evaluation.success_criteria: If survival models show consistently higher time-dependent AUC across varying follow-up windows compared to binary classifiers, supporting the hypothesis. If binary classifiers perform equally or better, refuting the hypothesis.

implementation_steps.description: Generate synthetic survival dataset with 1000 patients using Weibull distribution for time-to-event, incorporating baseline covariates (age, comorbidities, etc.) and random censoring
Implement Cox regression model using scikit-survival to fit survival data with censoring and calculate time-dependent AUC at multiple time points (15, 30, 60, 90 days)
Implement logistic regression model to predict binary readmission outcomes within fixed time windows (30 days) and calculate corresponding AUC
Compare time-dependent AUC values between survival and binary models across varying follow-up windows and report statistical significance of differences
Analyze results to determine whether survival models demonstrate superior discriminatory performance when follow-up windows vary, supporting or refuting the hypothesis

risks: Synthetic data may not perfectly replicate real-world readmission patterns
Time-dependent AUC calculation may be computationally intensive for large datasets
Potential overfitting in synthetic data generation leading to misleading results
